D2·svxw — 2026-09-15 — replaced by D28·h8vd
rule: Outcome capture adds only OPTIONAL exit/ok fields to command_run and file_touched in packages/schema/src; every richer observation is a diagnostics row whose shape also lives in packages/schema/src, never validates as an event envelope, and is referenced from the record only by id, hash or count.
chose: 1.1(a) — the outcome-capture SCHEMA contract, gating 1.2 and r1-fixes 2.5.
(1) Two shapes, one home. Both the durable outcome fields (event payloads) and the private diagnostics ROW shape live in packages/schema/src — event payloads in events.ts, the row shape in its own file (e.g. diagnostics.ts), exported from the package entry. Nothing in packages/engine defines or widens either shape.
(2) The split rule. DURABLE (an event in events.jsonl) is a fact the next session on ANY machine needs to resume, at the granularity a human write-back already states: that a command ran and whether it exited ok, that a file was touched. Concretely 1.2 may add OPTIONAL fields to the existing mechanical payloads — command_run gains exit status and an ok flag; file_touched gains an ok flag — and nothing more. Commit facts stay derived from git (commit-attribution: recorded in git, derived from git, never in the record), so r1-fixes 2.5's "commits with task-id prefix" is a read, not a capture. PRIVATE (a diagnostics row, never an event) is everything at tool-call granularity or richer: error text and stderr tails, is_error from the host, PostToolUseFailure payloads, MCP typed-error rejections, hook latency, bytes injected, digest size, memory citation signals, tool names and counts including read-only tools and self-recording git/sofar commands.
(3) Rows are structurally not events. A row carries no ulid `id` and its `kind` is never a member of EVENT_TYPES, so validateEnvelope rejects it by construction; a test pins this. The record may reference diagnostics only by opaque row id, content hash or aggregate count — never by content.
(4) Additive only. New durable fields are optional; an engine that predates them folds the event unchanged (the fold counts command_run and never reads cmd — that stays true). A consumer that finds a field absent reports UNKNOWN for it, never a default (1.3 owns the availability map).
(5) Redaction precedes storage on both sides: command text only through redactCommand; error text clipped to a fixed byte bound and redacted; no tool arguments, no transcripts, no absolute paths outside the clone root by default.
over: (a) A single rich `tool_outcome` event type in events.jsonl carrying exit code, is_error and error text — the audit's original 1.2 shape. (b) Keeping the row shape inside packages/engine next to the store code, since only the engine reads it. (c) A new `test_result` event that names pass/fail semantically.
because: Verified this session against main @ b29d013: core/cursor.ts exportEvents returns every envelope-valid event and client/push.ts pushStream ships that stream with no type filtering, so ANY event in events.jsonl reaches git and sync — a rich outcome event would put error text, which routinely carries paths and secrets, into every clone forever (security-hardening 3.1's argument for redactCommand applies with more force). CommandRunPayload today is {cmd} only, so exit status is genuinely missing from the record, and an optional exit/ok pair is the smallest addition that gives r1-fixes 2.5 its "test pass/fail" without inventing semantics — an exit code is a fact, "tests passed" is an interpretation the audit (S2) says exit codes cannot carry. CLAUDE.md's guard-rail puts schema ONLY in packages/schema/src, and the row shape is schema whatever its storage. r1-fixes ruled 2026-09-15 (its D-rule: never define outcome-capture payloads or storage in r1-fixes) that it consumes this contract, so there is exactly one owner.
